docs.text: HardFOC driver BNO08x Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the CEVA BNO080, BNO085 and BNO086 9-axis IMU with on-chip sensor fusion. It starts the SH-2 sensor hub, enables the reports you ask for and hands you quaternions, vectors and events, on any MCU with I2C, SPI or UART. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes over your bus, reports when the hub has data and drives a reset pin; it does the rest: the SH-2 session through CEVA's own SH-2 library, report decoding, re-enabling reports after a hub reset, the UART-RVC frame parser and firmware updates. 9-axis IMU with sensor-fusion hub BNO08x CEVA (formerly Hillcrest Labs) Sensors Accelerometer (±8 g), gyroscope (±2000 °/s) and magnetometer, fused on chip by the SH-2 firmware Outputs Rotation vectors up to 400 Hz (gyro-integrated up to 1 kHz), calibrated and raw IMU data, steps, taps, activity Host interface I2C up to 400 kHz (address 0x4A / 0x4B), SPI mode 3 up to 3 MHz, UART 3 Mbit/s, or UART-RVC 115200 Supply VDD 2.4 V to 3.6 V (sensors), VDDIO 1.7 V to 3.6 V (core and I/O) Package 28-pin LGA, 3.8 mm × 5.2 mm × 1.1 mm, −40 °C to 85 °C Driver modes SH-2 over I2C, SPI or UART; UART-RVC streaming; firmware update through the bootloader Datasheet · SH-2 reference manual · SHTP specification What you get ¶ One object per sensor. BNO085<YourPort> covers SH-2 reports, UART-RVC and firmware updates; the port's interface type decides which calls are allowed. See API guide . Every SH-2 report. 40 report types, from rotation vectors and calibrated IMU data to step counter, tap, stability and activity classifiers, decoded into one SensorEvent . See Configuration . Callbacks or polling. Register a callback, or ask HasNewData() and read GetLatest() ; both work at once. No threads inside: you call Update() . Survives hub resets. When the hub reports a reset, the driver re-enables every report you had configured. UART-RVC and firmware update. Heading, pitch, roll and acceleration at 100 Hz with no protocol stack ( UART-RVC mode ), and in-field firmware updates through the bootloader ( Firmware update ). Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class: no virtual calls, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: start the hub, enable reports, read them, stop, and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Imu standing for BNO085<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One BNO085<Comm> object per sensor. Its calls fall into four groups; the port's GetInterfaceType() decides which groups work: Group Calls Interface SH-2 session Begin() , Close() , Update() I2C, SPI, UART Reports EnableSensor() , DisableSensor() , SetCallback() , HasNewData() , GetLatest() I2C, SPI, UART UART-RVC BeginRvc() , ServiceRvc() , SetRvcCallback() , CloseRvc() UARTRVC ( UART-RVC mode ) Firmware update EnterBootloader() , Dfu() , DfuFromMemory() , RunDfuFromMemory() , ExitBootloaderAndReboot() I2C, SPI, UART ( Firmware update ) Pins and state HardwareReset() , SetBootPin() , SetWakePin() , SelectInterface() , GetState() , GetLastError() any Calls that can fail return bool (or an SH-2 status int for firmware updates) and never throw. After a false , GetLastError() holds the reason as an SH2_ERR_* code. Start the hub ¶ bool start_imu ( Imu & imu ) { imu . HardwareReset (); // optional: NRST low 2 ms, then 50 ms for the hub to boot if ( ! imu . Begin ()) { std :: printf ( "Begin failed: %d 
 " , imu . GetLastError ()); // SH2_ERR_* (sh2_err.h) return false ; } return imu . GetState () == BNO085DriverState :: Sh2Active ; } Begin() opens your port, starts the CEVA SH-2 library, waits up to 200 ms for the hub's reset message and sends a reinitialise command. Calling it again while the session is open returns true and does nothing. Enable reports ¶ bool enable_reports ( Imu & imu ) { bool ok = true ; ok &= imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: GameRotationVector , 5 ); // 200 Hz, no magnetometer ok &= imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: LinearAcceleration , 10 ); // 100 Hz ok &= imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: Gyroscope , 10 ); // 100 Hz ok &= imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: StepCounter , 0 ); // on change ok &= imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: TapDetector , 0 ); // on change return ok ; } EnableSensor(sensor, interval_ms, sensitivity) takes the report period in milliseconds; 0 suits on-change reports such as the step counter. The hub picks a rate between 0.9 and 2.1 times the one you ask for, and not every report can run at its maximum at once. The driver remembers each interval and re-sends it when the hub reports a reset. Configuration lists the report types and their maximum rates. Read reports with a callback ¶ void use_callbacks ( Imu & imu ) { imu . SetCallback ([]( const SensorEvent & e ) { switch ( e . sensor ) { case BNO085Sensor :: GameRotationVector : std :: printf ( "q %.3f %.3f %.3f %.3f 
 " , e . rotation . w , e . rotation . x , e . rotation . y , e . rotation . z ); break ; case BNO085Sensor :: StepCounter : std :: printf ( "steps %u 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( e . stepCount )); break ; case BNO085Sensor :: TapDetector : std :: printf ( "%s tap 
 " , e . tap . doubleTap ? "double" : "single" ); break ; default : break ; } }); for (;;) { imu . Update (); // the callback runs from here, on this thread } } The callback runs inside Update() , on the thread that calls it, once per report. Keep it short: copy the data out. SensorEvent is one struct for every report type; the fields that matter depend on e.sensor : Report Field Unit Rotation vectors ( RotationVector , GameRotationVector , GeomagneticRotationVector , ARVRStabilized* ) rotation (w, x, y, z, accuracy) unit quaternion GyroIntegratedRV rotation , angularVelocity quaternion, rad/s Accelerometer , LinearAcceleration , Gravity vector m/s² Gyroscope / GyroUncalibrated vector (+ bias ) rad/s Magnetometer / MagneticFieldUncalibrated vector (+ bias ) µT RawAccelerometer , RawGyroscope , RawMagnetometer raw ADC counts Pressure , AmbientLight , Humidity , Proximity , Temperature scalar hPa, lux, %, cm, °C StepCounter stepCount , latencyUs steps, µs TapDetector tap (doubleTap, direction) StabilityClassifier , PersonalActivityClassifier classification , activity Gesture detectors (shake, flip, pickup, tilt, ...) detected , eventFlags Read reports by polling ¶ void poll ( Imu & imu ) { imu . Update (); if ( imu . HasNewData ( BNO085Sensor :: LinearAcceleration )) { const SensorEvent e = imu . GetLatest ( BNO085Sensor :: LinearAcceleration ); // clears the flag std :: printf ( "a %.2f %.2f %.2f m/s^2 (accuracy %u) 
 " , e . vector . x , e . vector . y , e . vector . z , static_cast < unsigned > ( e . vector . accuracy )); } } HasNewData() is set when a report arrives and cleared by GetLatest() . The callback does not clear it, so you can mix both styles. Outside an SH-2 session HasNewData() returns false and GetLatest() a default event. Stop reports and close ¶ void stop ( Imu & imu ) { imu . DisableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: Gyroscope ); // report interval 0: the hub stops it imu . Close (); // sh2_close(), then the port's Close() } The destructor closes an open SH-2 or RVC session too. Close the session before you power the sensor down. Handle errors ¶ const char * sh2_error_name ( int code ) { switch ( code ) { case SH2_OK : return "ok" ; case SH2_ERR : return "general error (transport did not open, hub did not answer)" ; case SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM : return "bad parameter, or a call for the wrong interface type" ; case SH2_ERR_OP_IN_PROGRESS : return "wrong driver state (not started, or another mode is active)" ; case SH2_ERR_IO : return "bus error" ; case SH2_ERR_HUB : return "the hub reported an error" ; case SH2_ERR_TIMEOUT : return "the hub did not answer in time" ; default : return "unknown" ; } } bool enable_or_report ( Imu & imu ) { if ( ! imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: RotationVector , 10 )) { std :: printf ( "EnableSensor: %s 
 " , sh2_error_name ( imu . GetLastError ())); return false ; } return true ; } Signal Meaning Where to look Begin() is false , SH2_ERR The port's Open() failed, or the SH-2 library could not start Bus pins, address, power SH2_ERR_TIMEOUT The hub did not answer a command in time H_INTN wiring, Read() contract, PS0/PS1 straps SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM Wrong interface for the call (SH-2 call on UART-RVC, or the reverse), or a bad DFU image GetInterfaceType() SH2_ERR_OP_IN_PROGRESS Wrong state: reports before Begin() , a call during a firmware update GetState() accuracy 0 or 1 Calibration not settled yet Move the device; keep it away from magnetic fields Reports stop, then resume The hub reset; the driver re-enabled your reports Supply, NRST, ESD Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes. Control pins ¶ HardwareReset(lowMs) holds NRST active for lowMs (default 2 ms) and then waits 50 ms. SetBootPin(true) asserts BOOTN (low) for the bootloader; SetWakePin(true) asserts WAKE in SPI mode. Each forwards to your port's GpioSet() , so a pin the board does not wire is a no-op. Hardware has the levels.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: the layers, the CEVA SH-2 library underneath, and how one call reaches the hub. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one BNO085 object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bno08x.hpp. In SH-2 mode the core hands every transfer to the CEVA SH-2 and SHTP library (the src/sh2 submodule); in UART-RVC mode it parses the 19-byte frames itself; firmware updates use the bootloader protocol in the core. Both paths end in the communication interface (bno08x::CommInterface in inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp), a CRTP base whose methods your platform port implements: move bytes, report data-ready, wait, keep time and drive the control pins. Below it is the sensor hub. Drawn from: inc/bno08x.hpp BNO085 public members ; inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp CommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : BNO085<Comm> inc/bno08x.hpp Interface, SH-2 library Never CEVA SH-2 and SHTP library src/sh2/ sh2_Hal_t from the core For CEVA fixes Communication interface : bno08x::CommInterface<Derived> inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp Your port Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Per MCU ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test mock. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the hub ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as BNO085 core participant S as SH-2 library participant P as Your port A->>D: EnableSensor(RotationVector, 10) D->>D: cache 10 000 µs for re-enable after a reset D->>S: sh2_setSensorConfig(id, interval_us) S->>P: Write(Set Feature transfer) A->>D: Update() D->>S: sh2_service() S->>P: Read(buffer, 1024) P-->>S: one SHTP transfer (or 0) S-->>D: sensorCallback(event) D->>D: decode into SensorEvent, set the new-data flag D-->>A: your callback(SensorEvent) The SH-2 library calls the port through a C function table ( sh2_Hal_t : open , close , read , write , getTimeUs ). The core fills it with static trampolines that forward to your port's Open() , Close() , Read() , Write() and GetTimeUs() . Three modes, one object ¶ The port's GetInterfaceType() decides what the object may do, and a small state machine ( BNO085DriverState ) keeps the modes apart: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Closed Closed --> Sh2Active: Begin() (I2C, SPI, UART) Sh2Active --> Closed: Close() Closed --> RvcActive: BeginRvc() (UARTRVC) RvcActive --> Closed: Close() / CloseRvc() Closed --> DfuInProgress: Dfu...() (I2C, SPI, UART) Sh2Active --> DfuInProgress: Dfu...() closes SH-2 first DfuInProgress --> Closed: transfer done or failed A call for the wrong interface fails with SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM ; a call in the wrong state fails with SH2_ERR_OP_IN_PROGRESS . GetLastError() returns the code. Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The interface is a template parameter. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them: no vtable, no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: BNO085<MyI2c> . CEVA's library, unmodified. The SH-2 protocol (sensor configuration, FRS records, report decoding) is CEVA's own code, kept as a submodule. The core adds the C++ types, the report cache and the reset handling. A latest-value cache. Each of the 47 possible sensor IDs keeps its last decoded value and a new-data flag, so callbacks and polling work together. One SH-2 session per program. The CEVA library keeps its state in a single global instance, so one BNO085 object can run SH-2 at a time. UART-RVC objects do not use the library and have no such limit. Not thread-safe. Call one driver object from one task, or guard it with a mutex. docs.text: The port's GetInterfaceType() decides what the object may do, and a small state machine ( BNO085DriverState ) keeps the modes apart: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Closed Closed --> Sh2Active: Begin() (I2C, SPI, UART) Sh2Active --> Closed: Close() Closed --> RvcActive: BeginRvc() (UARTRVC) RvcActive --> Closed: Close() / CloseRvc() Closed --> DfuInProgress: Dfu...() (I2C, SPI, UART) Sh2Active --> DfuInProgress: Dfu...() closes SH-2 first DfuInProgress --> Closed: transfer done or failed A call for the wrong interface fails with SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM ; a call in the wrong state fails with SH2_ERR_OP_IN_PROGRESS . docs.text: CRTP, not virtual functions. The interface is a template parameter. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them: no vtable, no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: BNO085<MyI2c> . CEVA's library, unmodified. The SH-2 protocol (sensor configuration, FRS records, report decoding) is CEVA's own code, kept as a submodule. The core adds the C++ types, the report cache and the reset handling. A latest-value cache. Each of the 47 possible sensor IDs keeps its last decoded value and a new-data flag, so callbacks and polling work together. One SH-2 session per program. The CEVA library keeps its state in a single global instance, so one BNO085 object can run SH-2 at a time. UART-RVC objects do not use the library and have no such limit. Not thread-safe. Call one driver object from one task, or guard it with a mutex.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ The settings a BNO08x needs: which reports at which rates, the pins sampled at reset, and the limits of the hub. Every snippet here is compiled from tests/docs/configuration.cpp . The driver has no configuration struct: the hub is configured per report with EnableSensor() , and the board with straps. Report rates ¶ bool configure_reports ( BNO085 < MyI2c >& imu ) { // interval_ms: period between reports. The hub picks a rate between 0.9x and 2.1x the request. // sensitivity: for on-change reports, the change that triggers a report; 0 disables the filter. return imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: RotationVector , 10 ) // 100 Hz, 9-axis && imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: GyroIntegratedRV , 2 ) // 500 Hz, up to 1 kHz && imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: Accelerometer , 4 ) // 250 Hz, up to 500 Hz && imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: Magnetometer , 20 ) // 50 Hz, up to 100 Hz && imu . EnableSensor ( BNO085Sensor :: StabilityClassifier , 0 ); // on change } Argument Meaning interval_ms Report period. The driver sends interval_ms × 1000 µs; the hub runs between 0.9 and 2.1 times the requested rate sensitivity For on-change reports, the change that triggers a report, rounded to an integer and clamped to 0 ... 65535; 0 turns the filter off The driver does not expose batching or the sensor-specific configuration word: it sends a batch interval of 0 and sensorSpecific = 0 . Use the SH-2 library's sh2_setSensorConfig() directly if you need them. Maximum rates ¶ From the datasheet (figure 6-16). Each report can run at its maximum on its own; all of them at once cannot, so balance high and low rates against the bus bandwidth and the hub's processing. The SH-2 reference manual defines each report. Pins sampled at reset ¶ void select_interface_and_reset ( BNO085 < MyI2c >& imu ) { imu . SetBootPin ( false ); // BOOTN high: boot the application, not the bootloader imu . HardwareReset ( 10 ); // NRST low 10 ms; PS0, PS1, BOOTN and SA0 are sampled now } Pin Selects Typical strap PS0, PS1 Host interface ( Hardware ) Both to GND for I2C SA0 I2C address bit 0: 0x4A or 0x4B GND or VDDIO BOOTN Application or bootloader 10 kΩ to VDDIO; a GPIO for firmware updates CLKSEL0, CLKSEL1 Internal oscillator, external crystal or external clock Board-specific; UART modes need the crystal or clock Accuracy ¶ Rotation vectors and calibrated vectors carry an accuracy from 0 to 3: unreliable, low, medium, high. docs.text: Firmware update ¶ Replace the BNO08x's SH-2 firmware in the field through its bootloader, with an image you supply. Use an image from CEVA for your exact part A wrong or interrupted image leaves the hub in the bootloader. Keep BOOTN on a GPIO so you can always re-enter it, keep the supply stable during the transfer, and check that the image's part number matches your part. What the bootloader needs ¶ BOOTN low at reset. The bootloader samples BOOTN with PS0 and PS1 when NRST rises. Wire BOOTN to a GPIO (with its 10 kΩ pull-up) and NRST to another. I2C, SPI or UART. The bootloader uses the interface the PS pins select; UART-RVC has no bootloader mode, so the DFU calls fail with SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM on a UARTRVC port. A different I2C address. Over I2C the bootloader answers at 0x28 (SA0 low) or 0x29 (SA0 high), not 0x4A / 0x4B . The driver does not switch addresses: your port must talk to the bootloader address between EnterBootloader() and ExitBootloaderAndReboot() . A vendor image. CEVA supplies BNO08x firmware as an HcBin image with metadata ( FW-Format , SW-Part-Number ). The image compiled in from src/dfu/firmware-bno.c is a 64-byte stub that the driver refuses. Update from memory ¶ int update_firmware ( MyI2c & bus , const uint8_t * image , uint32_t size ) { BNO085 < MyI2c > imu ( bus ); DfuMemoryImage fw {}; fw . data = image ; fw . length = size ; fw . format = "BNO_V1" ; // FW-Format of the vendor image fw . partNumber = "1000-3608" ; // SW-Part-Number of the vendor image DfuOptions options {}; options . progress = []( const DfuProgress & p ) { std :: printf ( "%u / %u bytes \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( p . bytesSent ), static_cast < unsigned > ( p . totalBytes )); }; // BOOTN low across a reset, transfer, then BOOTN high and reset into the application. const int status = imu . RunDfuFromMemory ( fw , options ); if ( status != SH2_OK ) { return status ; } return imu . Begin () ? SH2_OK : imu . GetLastError (); } RunDfuFromMemory() does the whole sequence and returns SH2_OK (0) or a negative SH-2 code: Enter the bootloader. EnterBootloader(10, 50) : close any open session, open the port, assert BOOTN, hold NRST low 10 ms, wait 50 ms, release BOOTN, wait 50 ms. Check the image. FW-Format must be BNO_V1 and SW-Part-Number a known part (or the one you require), and the image at least 1024 bytes; otherwise SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM before anything is sent. Send the size. The application length as 4 bytes big-endian plus CRC-16, then the packet length (1 to 64 bytes) plus CRC-16. The bootloader acknowledges each with s . Send the image. Packets of up to 64 bytes, each with a CRC-16 (CCITT, polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF), each acknowledged; up to 5 attempts and 100 ms per packet. options.progress runs after each one. Reboot. ExitBootloaderAndReboot(2, 100) : BOOTN high, NRST low 2 ms, wait 50 ms plus 100 ms. Then call Begin() as usual. Options ¶ DfuOptions field Default Effect requireFormatMatch true Check the image's FW-Format against requiredFormat requiredFormat "BNO_V1" Expected format requirePartNumber true Check SW-Part-Number against requiredPartNumber , or, when that is null, against the known part numbers 1000-3608 , 1000-3676 , 1000-4148 , 1000-4563 requiredPartNumber nullptr Exact part number to require packetLenOverride 0 Packet length 1 to 64; 0 uses the image's preference, capped at 64 progress empty Called with 0 bytes before the first packet, then after each packet DfuMemoryImage describes a raw image in memory: data , length , format , partNumber and an optional preferredPacketLen . For an image you stream from storage, implement the HcBin_t function table ( src/dfu/HcBin.h ) and call DfuWithOptions(image, options) between the bootloader calls. Step by step ¶ Call the pieces yourself when you need to do something between them, such as switching the I2C address: Call Does EnterBootloader(resetLowMs = 10, settleMs = 50) BOOTN + reset sequence above; false on a UARTRVC port or during a transfer DfuFromMemory(image, options) Steps 2 to 4 from a DfuMemoryImage DfuWithOptions(hcbin, options) / Dfu(hcbin) Steps 2 to 4 from any HcBin_t ; Dfu() uses the default options ExitBootloaderAndReboot(resetLowMs = 2, settleMs = 100) BOOTN released, reset, wait During the transfer GetState() is DfuInProgress and Close() is refused. A transfer that starts while an SH-2 session is open closes the session first. Next ¶ The dfu_update and dfu_workflow_test ESP32 apps run this on hardware; Hardware has the BOOTN and NRST wiring.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a BNO08x, with which bus settings, and the board-level traps to avoid. All values here come from the BNO08X datasheet (CEVA 1000-3927, revision 1.17). Pin numbers are the 28-pin LGA's; a breakout board names them on its silkscreen and often straps some of them. When the datasheet and a board's schematic disagree, the schematic wins for what is strapped. Host interface pins ¶ Signal Pin Direction (chip) I2C SPI UART / UART-RVC H_SCL / SCK / RX 19 in / bidirectional SCL SCK RX (host to chip) H_SDA / H_MISO / TX 20 bidirectional / out SDA MISO TX (chip to host) SA0 / H_MOSI 17 in Address bit 0 MOSI n/a H_CSN 18 in n/a Chip select, active low n/a H_INTN 14 out Data ready, active low Data ready, active low Asserted about 7.7 µs before each UART message (UART-SHTP) Control pins ¶ The driver addresses these by name ( bno08x::CtrlPin ) and by state ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE ); your port maps a state to a level. ACTIVE means "function asserted", which is a low level on the three active-low pins. Pin CtrlPin Direction (chip) What it does Driver use NRST (11) RSTN in Active-low reset HardwareReset() , EnterBootloader() , ExitBootloaderAndReboot() BOOTN (4) BOOTN in Low at reset: start the bootloader. Pull up through 10 kΩ SetBootPin() , the bootloader helpers PS0 / WAKE (6) PS0 , WAKE in Protocol select bit 0 at reset; in SPI mode, an active-low wake afterwards SelectInterface() , SetWakePin() PS1 (5) PS1 in Protocol select bit 1 at reset SelectInterface() Protocol selection ¶ PS1, PS0 and BOOTN are sampled at reset (datasheet figure 1-5). Strap them, or drive them before you release NRST. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 driver over CEVA's SH-2 library, which is compiled C. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler (GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC) and a C99 compiler for the SH-2 library. The CEVA SH-2 library in the src/sh2 submodule (Apache-2.0). No RTOS and no exceptions. The driver uses std::function for callbacks, which may allocate when you store a capturing lambda that does not fit its small buffer. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose. Initialise src/sh2 too: the build needs it. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-bno08x-driver.git external/hf-bno08x-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-bno08x-driver/src/sh2 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-bno08x-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_bno08x ) # or the alias hf::bno08x The hf_bno08x target is a static library of the SH-2 sources and the DFU firmware stub. It carries the include directories ( inc/ , src/ , src/dfu/ , src/sh2/ and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_BNO08X_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on the library sources HF_BNO08X_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) Use the driver from source with add_subdirectory() . The install rules copy only inc/ , while bno08x.hpp includes src/bno08x.ipp and the SH-2 headers, so an installed package does not compile yet. ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_bno08x/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_BNO08X_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_bno08x . The wrapper compiles the same sources and requires the driver and freertos components. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_bno08x_build_settings.cmake Sources, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt Static library for host builds, install rules and CI ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_bno08x/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into bno08x_version.h at configure time. Read it at run time: const char * v = GetBNO08xDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0"; also BNO085<MyI2c>::GetDriverVersion() Firmware image for updates ¶ src/dfu/firmware-bno.c defines the image Dfu() uses by default. It is a 64-byte stub that the driver refuses (an image must be at least 1024 bytes). For firmware updates, pass a vendor image at run time with DfuFromMemory() , or replace this file with the vendor's. See Firmware update . Next ¶ Quickstart wires the sensor and reads orientation; Porting writes the communication interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the communication interface for your bus. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls nine methods on a class you derive from bno08x::CommInterface<Self> (in inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions and no vtable. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one BNO085 object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bno08x.hpp. In SH-2 mode the core hands every transfer to the CEVA SH-2 and SHTP library (the src/sh2 submodule); in UART-RVC mode it parses the 19-byte frames itself; firmware updates use the bootloader protocol in the core. Both paths end in the communication interface (bno08x::CommInterface in inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp), a CRTP base whose methods your platform port implements: move bytes, report data-ready, wait, keep time and drive the control pins. Below it is the sensor hub. Drawn from: inc/bno08x.hpp BNO085 public members ; inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp CommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Called by Contract GetInterfaceType() Begin() , BeginRvc() , the DFU calls Return I2C , SPI , UART or UARTRVC ; it decides which calls are allowed Open() Begin() , BeginRvc() , the bootloader helpers, DFU Initialise the bus and pins. May be called again while open: return true without re-initialising Close() Close() , CloseRvc() , the end of a DFU transfer Release the bus Write(data, length) SH-2 library, DFU Send one SHTP transfer (or DFU packet). Return the bytes accepted, 0 if the bus is busy, negative on error Read(data, length) SH-2 library, RVC parser, DFU SH-2: return one complete SHTP transfer, header included, or 0 when there is none. RVC: return whatever bytes have arrived, without blocking DataAvailable() your port, usually inside Read() true when H_INTN is low; true always when there is no interrupt line Delay(ms) reset and bootloader sequences Block for at least ms milliseconds GetTimeUs() SH-2 timestamps and timeouts, RVC timestamps A monotonic 32-bit microsecond counter; wrapping is fine GpioSet(pin, signal) HardwareReset() , SetBootPin() , SetWakePin() , SelectInterface() Drive RSTN , BOOTN , WAKE , PS0 , PS1 ; ignore pins the board does not wire GpioSetActive(pin) and GpioSetInactive(pin) come with the base class. I2C port ¶ my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public bno08x :: CommInterface < MyI2c > { public : static constexpr uint8_t kAddress = 0x4A ; // SA0 low; 0x4B with SA0 high static constexpr int kIntnGpio = 17 ; // H_INTN, active low static constexpr int kRstnGpio = 16 ; // NRST, active low static constexpr int kBootnGpio = 18 ; // BOOTN, active low (optional, for firmware updates) BNO085Interface GetInterfaceType () noexcept { return BNO085Interface :: I2C ; } // Called by Begin() and the bootloader helpers, possibly more than once: initialise once. bool Open () noexcept { if ( ! open_ ) { open_ = platform_i2c_open ( 400000 ); // standard 100 kHz or fast 400 kHz } return open_ ; } void Close () noexcept { platform_i2c_close (); open_ = false ; } // One SHTP transfer from the SH-2 library. Return the bytes accepted, or a negative value. int Write ( const uint8_t * data , uint32_t length ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( kAddress , data , length ) ? static_cast < int > ( length ) : -1 ; } // Return one complete SHTP transfer (header included), 0 when the hub has nothing to send. int Read ( uint8_t * data , uint32_t length ) noexcept { if ( ! DataAvailable ()) { return 0 ; } uint8_t header [ 4 ]; if ( ! platform_i2c_read ( kAddress , header , sizeof ( header ))) { return -1 ; } uint32_t transfer = ( header [ 0 ] | ( header [ 1 ] << 8 )) & 0x7FFFU ; // bit 15: continuation flag if ( transfer == 0 ) { return 0 ; // empty transfer } if ( transfer > length ) { transfer = length ; } // A new read starts again at the header, so read the whole transfer. return platform_i2c_read ( kAddress , data , transfer ) ? static_cast < int > ( transfer ) : -1 ; } // H_INTN low: the hub has a transfer waiting. bool DataAvailable () noexcept { return ! platform_gpio_read ( kIntnGpio ); } void Delay ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } uint32_t GetTimeUs () noexcept { return platform_micros (); } // ACTIVE means "function asserted": low on NRST and BOOTN. PS0/PS1 are strapped to GND for I2C. void GpioSet ( bno08x :: CtrlPin pin , bno08x :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = signal == bno08x :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case bno08x :: CtrlPin :: RSTN : platform_gpio_write ( kRstnGpio , ! active ); break ; case bno08x :: CtrlPin :: BOOTN : platform_gpio_write ( kBootnGpio , ! active ); break ; case bno08x :: CtrlPin :: WAKE : case bno08x :: CtrlPin :: PS0 : case bno08x :: CtrlPin :: PS1 : break ; // not wired on this board } } private : bool open_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: Plain transactions. One START ... STOP per call, no register address, no repeated start. Read the length, then the transfer. Bits 0 to 14 of the 4-byte SHTP header are the transfer length, header included; bit 15 marks a continuation. On I2C every read starts at the header again, so read 4 bytes, then the whole length. A zero length is an empty transfer (BNO086 sends them when it has nothing): return 0. Gate on H_INTN. Reading when the hub has nothing makes a BNO085 stretch the clock until it does. Return a negative value only for a bus failure. The SH-2 library handles protocol errors. UART-RVC port ¶ my_rvc.hpp class MyRvcUart : public bno08x :: CommInterface < MyRvcUart > { public : static constexpr int kRstnGpio = 16 ; // NRST, active low (optional) BNO085Interface GetInterfaceType () noexcept { return BNO085Interface :: UARTRVC ; } bool Open () noexcept { return platform_uart_open ( 115200 ); } void Close () noexcept { platform_uart_close (); } // RVC is transmit-only on the sensor side: the driver never writes. int Write ( const uint8_t * /*data*/ , uint32_t /*length*/ ) noexcept { return 0 ; } // Non-blocking: whatever the UART has received, up to length bytes. ServiceRvc() calls it until // it returns 0. int Read ( uint8_t * data , uint32_t length ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , length ); } // No interrupt line in RVC mode. bool DataAvailable () noexcept { return true ; } void Delay ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } uint32_t GetTimeUs () noexcept { return platform_micros (); } void GpioSet ( bno08x :: CtrlPin pin , bno08x :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin == bno08x :: CtrlPin :: RSTN ) { platform_gpio_write ( kRstnGpio , signal != bno08x :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } } }; ServiceRvc() calls Read(&byte, 1) until it returns 0, so Read() must not block. Give the UART a receive buffer of a few frames (19 bytes each, one every 10 ms) so nothing is lost between calls. SPI and UART-SHTP ports ¶ The driver supports both through the same interface: report SPI or UART from GetInterfaceType() and keep the Read() contract (one complete SHTP transfer). The repository has no reference port for either yet. Points to cover: SPI UART Mode 3, MSB first, up to 3 MHz. Wait for H_INTN low before you assert H_CSN. SPI is full duplex: the hub may send while you write. Read the 4-byte header first to learn the length, and follow the SHTP specification for the SPI framing. Map CtrlPin::WAKE to the PS0/WAKE GPIO: drive it low to wake the hub before a write. 3 Mbit/s, 8N1, with an external 32.768 kHz clock or crystal on the BNO08x. SHTP over UART adds framing bytes around each transfer; see the SHTP specification . Leave at least 100 µs between bytes sent to the hub. Control-pin levels ¶ GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "function asserted". On the BNO08x that is a low level for NRST, BOOTN and WAKE, and a high level (logic 1) for PS0 and PS1. Your GpioSet() applies the board's levels; inverters or level shifters change them. Pin ACTIVE level on the chip Board without the pin RSTN low Tie NRST to the board reset; HardwareReset() then only waits BOOTN low Pull up through 10 kΩ; no firmware updates WAKE low Not needed on I2C or UART PS0 , PS1 high Strap them ( Hardware ) Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_bno08x_bus.hpp , an ESP-IDF i2c_master port with H_INTN and NRST, and esp32_uart_rvc_bus.hpp for UART-RVC. Start from them for an ESP-IDF target. The I2C reference reads the whole 1024-byte buffer on every Read() ; the header-first read on this page moves far fewer bytes. Check your port ¶ Build it: both ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Watch H_INTN after HardwareReset() : it goes low about 94 ms after NRST rises when the strapping is right. Begin() returns true : the SH-2 library received the hub's reset message and a reply to a command. Enable RotationVector at 10 ms and count reports for a second: about 100 means reads keep up. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe, and the CEVA SH-2 library keeps one global session. Give the sensor one owner task that calls Update() , or guard every call on the driver object (and its port) with one mutex.

Your application talks to one BNO085 object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bno08x.hpp. In SH-2 mode the core hands every transfer to the CEVA SH-2 and SHTP library (the src/sh2 submodule); in UART-RVC mode it parses the 19-byte frames itself; firmware updates use the bootloader protocol in the core. Both paths end in the communication interface (bno08x::CommInterface in inc/bno08x_comm_interface.hpp), a CRTP base whose methods your platform port implements: move bytes, report data-ready, wait, keep time and drive the control pins. docs.text: The driver supports both through the same interface: report SPI or UART from GetInterfaceType() and keep the Read() contract (one complete SHTP transfer). The repository has no reference port for either yet. Points to cover: SPI UART Mode 3, MSB first, up to 3 MHz. Wait for H_INTN low before you assert H_CSN. SPI is full duplex: the hub may send while you write. Read the 4-byte header first to learn the length, and follow the SHTP specification for the SPI framing. Map CtrlPin::WAKE to the PS0/WAKE GPIO: drive it low to wake the hub before a write. 3 Mbit/s, 8N1, with an external 32.768 kHz clock or crystal on the BNO08x. SHTP over UART adds framing bytes around each transfer; see the SHTP specification . Leave at least 100 µs between bytes sent to the hub.

docs.text: UART-RVC mode ¶ Heading, pitch, roll and acceleration at 100 Hz over one UART line, with no protocol stack and no commands. UART-RVC is a simplified output mode CEVA designed for ground robots such as robot vacuum cleaners. The hub sends a fixed 19-byte frame every 10 ms and listens to nothing. You cannot choose reports, change the rate or update firmware in this mode; for any of that, use SH-2 over I2C, SPI or UART. Select it ¶ Strap PS1 low and PS0 high, then reset (datasheet figure 1-5). The UART runs at 115200 bit/s, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, and needs the external 32.768 kHz crystal or clock: the internal oscillator is not accurate enough. Only the chip's TX pin (pin 20) is used; connect it to your MCU's RX. Use it ¶ The port reports BNO085Interface::UARTRVC and returns received bytes from Read() without blocking: my_rvc.hpp class MyRvcUart : public bno08x :: CommInterface < MyRvcUart > { public : static constexpr int kRstnGpio = 16 ; // NRST, active low (optional) BNO085Interface GetInterfaceType () noexcept { return BNO085Interface :: UARTRVC ; } bool Open () noexcept { return platform_uart_open ( 115200 ); } void Close () noexcept { platform_uart_close (); } // RVC is transmit-only on the sensor side: the driver never writes. int Write ( const uint8_t * /*data*/ , uint32_t /*length*/ ) noexcept { return 0 ; } // Non-blocking: whatever the UART has received, up to length bytes. ServiceRvc() calls it until // it returns 0. int Read ( uint8_t * data , uint32_t length ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , length ); } // No interrupt line in RVC mode. bool DataAvailable () noexcept { return true ; } void Delay ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } uint32_t GetTimeUs () noexcept { return platform_micros (); } void GpioSet ( bno08x :: CtrlPin pin , bno08x :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin == bno08x :: CtrlPin :: RSTN ) { platform_gpio_write ( kRstnGpio , signal != bno08x :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } } }; int stream_heading ( MyRvcUart & uart ) { BNO085 < MyRvcUart > imu ( uart ); imu . SetRvcCallback ([]( const RvcSensorValue & v ) { std :: printf ( "#%u yaw %.2f pitch %.2f roll %.2f deg a %.3f %.3f %.3f g \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( v . index ), v . yaw_deg , v . pitch_deg , v . roll_deg , v . acc_x_g , v . acc_y_g , v . acc_z_g ); }); if ( ! imu . BeginRvc ()) { // opens the UART; fails unless the port reports UARTRVC return imu . GetLastError (); } for (;;) { imu . ServiceRvc (); // parse what has arrived; one frame every 10 ms uart . Delay ( 5 ); } } BeginRvc() opens the port and starts the parser; it fails with SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM on any other interface type. ServiceRvc() reads every byte that has arrived and calls your callback once per valid frame. CloseRvc() (or Close() ) closes the port. SH-2 calls on an RVC object fail the same way, so one object cannot mix the modes. Frame format ¶ Offset Bytes Field Unit RvcSensorValue 0 2 Header 0xAA 0xAA 2 1 Index, counts 0 to 255 index 3 2 Yaw, little-endian int16 , ±180° 0.01° yaw_deg 5 2 Pitch, ±90° 0.01° pitch_deg 7 2 Roll, ±180° 0.01° roll_deg 9 2 X acceleration mg acc_x_g 11 2 Y acceleration mg acc_y_g 13 2 Z acceleration mg acc_z_g 15 1 Motion intent (BNO086; reserved otherwise) mi 16 1 Motion request (BNO086; reserved otherwise) mr 17 1 Reserved, zero 18 1 Checksum: 8-bit sum of bytes 2 to 17 Yaw is measured from the orientation at reset. Apply the rotations in the order yaw, pitch, roll. The driver converts to degrees and g ( RvcSensorValue ) and stamps each frame with GetTimeUs() . The datasheet's example frame, AA AA DE 01 00 92 FF 25 08 8D FE EC FF D1 03 00 00 00 E7 , decodes to index 222, yaw 0.01°, pitch −1.10°, roll 20.85° and acceleration (−0.371, −0.020, 0.977) g. The host tests feed exactly this frame to the parser ( Testing and CI ). How the parser finds frames ¶ The parser keeps a 19-byte sliding window. Each byte shifts the window; when it starts with 0xAA 0xAA and the checksum matches, the frame is decoded, the callback runs and the window empties. A frame with a wrong checksum is skipped and the window keeps sliding, so the parser recovers by itself after noise or a partial frame. docs.text: The port reports BNO085Interface::UARTRVC and returns received bytes from Read() without blocking: my_rvc.hpp class MyRvcUart : public bno08x :: CommInterface < MyRvcUart > { public : static constexpr int kRstnGpio = 16 ; // NRST, active low (optional) BNO085Interface GetInterfaceType () noexcept { return BNO085Interface :: UARTRVC ; } bool Open () noexcept { return platform_uart_open ( 115200 ); } void Close () noexcept { platform_uart_close (); } // RVC is transmit-only on the sensor side: the driver never writes. int Write ( const uint8_t * /*data*/ , uint32_t /*length*/ ) noexcept { return 0 ; } // Non-blocking: whatever the UART has received, up to length bytes. ServiceRvc() calls it until // it returns 0. int Read ( uint8_t * data , uint32_t length ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , length ); } // No interrupt line in RVC mode. bool DataAvailable () noexcept { return true ; } void Delay ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } uint32_t GetTimeUs () noexcept { return platform_micros (); } void GpioSet ( bno08x :: CtrlPin pin , bno08x :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin == bno08x :: CtrlPin :: RSTN ) { platform_gpio_write ( kRstnGpio , signal != bno08x :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } } }; int stream_heading ( MyRvcUart & uart ) { BNO085 < MyRvcUart > imu ( uart ); imu . SetRvcCallback ([]( const RvcSensorValue & v ) { std :: printf ( "#%u yaw %.2f pitch %.2f roll %.2f deg a %.3f %.3f %.3f g \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( v . index ), v . yaw_deg , v . pitch_deg , v . roll_deg , v . acc_x_g , v . acc_y_g , v . acc_z_g ); }); if ( ! imu . BeginRvc ()) { // opens the UART; fails unless the port reports UARTRVC return imu . GetLastError (); } for (;;) { imu . ServiceRvc (); // parse what has arrived; one frame every 10 ms uart . Delay ( 5 ); } } BeginRvc() opens the port and starts the parser; it fails with SH2_ERR_BAD_PARAM on any other interface type. ServiceRvc() reads every byte that has arrived and calls your callback once per valid frame. CloseRvc() (or Close() ) closes the port. SH-2 calls on an RVC object fail the same way, so one object cannot mix the modes.
docs.title: Use it

docs.text: Offset Bytes Field Unit RvcSensorValue 0 2 Header 0xAA 0xAA 2 1 Index, counts 0 to 255 index 3 2 Yaw, little-endian int16 , ±180° 0.01° yaw_deg 5 2 Pitch, ±90° 0.01° pitch_deg 7 2 Roll, ±180° 0.01° roll_deg 9 2 X acceleration mg acc_x_g 11 2 Y acceleration mg acc_y_g 13 2 Z acceleration mg acc_z_g 15 1 Motion intent (BNO086; reserved otherwise) mi 16 1 Motion request (BNO086; reserved otherwise) mr 17 1 Reserved, zero 18 1 Checksum: 8-bit sum of bytes 2 to 17 Yaw is measured from the orientation at reset. Apply the rotations in the order yaw, pitch, roll. The driver converts to degrees and g ( RvcSensorValue ) and stamps each frame with GetTimeUs() . The datasheet's example frame, AA AA DE 01 00 92 FF 25 08 8D FE EC FF D1 03 00 00 00 E7 , decodes to index 222, yaw 0.01°, pitch −1.10°, roll 20.85° and acceleration (−0.371, −0.020, 0.977) g. The host tests feed exactly this frame to the parser ( Testing and CI ).
docs.title: Frame format

docs.text: The parser keeps a 19-byte sliding window. Each byte shifts the window; when it starts with 0xAA 0xAA and the checksum matches, the frame is decoded, the callback runs and the window empties. A frame with a wrong checksum is skipped and the window keeps sliding, so the parser recovers by itself after noise or a partial frame.

Your application talks to one BNO085 object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bno08x.hpp. In SH-2 mode the core hands every transfer to the CEVA SH-2 and SHTP library (the src/sh2 submodule); in UART-RVC mode it parses the 19-byte frames itself; firmware updates use the bootloader protocol in the core.
